caption: B, nothing picked yet. The page opens here: one section per repository, each naming its own default branch. Above the list, gitlab.fnt.example has a band of its own with Connect GitLab, so it isn’t a line of footer text.
B with engine on fix/redirects: engine’s section marks the branch, the other four stay on their defaults, and the chip and summary read “engine: fix/redirects · 4 on defaults”.
A, the same pick: the top row is “Default branches”, every repository is named with its branch, and engine’s fix/redirects stands out. The host band is the same band here.

C, the same pick: the run board. Repositories expand in place on the left, and “Where each run starts” on the right says engine runs fix/redirects on localhost:4100 while the other four keep their defaults.

The host band on its own: the GitLab mark, gitlab.fnt.example in mono, “Merge requests need a connection”, and a real Connect GitLab button. The host name truncates rather than pushing the button out.
Shared main with GitLab connected: all five defaults agree, the band is gone, and pull requests appear with the repository they belong to. frontend’s !18 is picked; the other four stay on main.
One repository: the picker falls back to today’s shape — main, tasks, branches — with no repository names or grouping; only the host band is added.
Connect GitLab in the band opens the token dialog for gitlab.fnt.example. Connecting turns the host on and fills the pull requests in.
